verdict: Spotify grew revenue 16% to €5.0B (about $5.6B) as Premium subscribers hit 306 million, and a record 33% gross margin turned that growth into €672M of operating income.

segments.name: Premium
segments.note: Subscriptions — 306 million people paying monthly, up 9% YoY, with price rises lifting revenue per user (ARPU) to €4.95.

segments.name: Ad-Supported
segments.note: The free tier's advertising business — ads sold against free listening, increasingly through automated channels.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the app, recommendation systems and new formats like video podcasts and audiobooks.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Winning listeners and advertisers — spending rose sharply this quarter on growth campaigns.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

takeaways.title: Subscriptions carry the business
takeaways.text: Premium is 90% of revenue and grew 17% — 306M subscribers, with price rises lifting revenue per user. The free, ad-funded tier is the funnel, not the engine.

takeaways.title: A record gross margin
takeaways.text: Gross margin hit a Q3 record 33.0% — Premium kept more of each euro as revenue grew faster than the music licensing costs it pays out.

takeaways.title: Cash keeps piling up
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was €735M in the quarter and the cash pile reached €9.9B — even as operating costs rose 26% on marketing and cloud/AI spending.

oneTimers: Operating expenses included €22M of 'social charges' — Swedish payroll taxes on share-based pay that swing with Spotify's share price; they came in €13M above forecast.
otherDetail: Finance items netted +$37M — interest earned on Spotify's large cash pile, minus finance costs (€33M as reported).
footerNote: Spotify reports in euros under IFRS. Dollar figures are converted at €1 = $1.1328 (USD:Euro 0.8828 at Sep 30, 2026, the rate in Spotify's own release). As reported: revenue €4,969M · gross profit €1,639M · operating income €672M · net income €518M.
